Incident Report INC-4471 — Redwood Payments
Severity: SEV-2 | Duration: 27 minutes | Date: May 9

Summary: Outbound webhook delivery for payment-confirmation events failed for all merchants between 03:14 and 03:41 UTC.

Root cause: The TLS certificate for webhooks.redwoodpay.com expired at 03:14 UTC. Auto-renewal had been disabled in March during a DNS provider migration and was never re-enabled.

Investigation notes: On-call engineer Nadia Petrov initially suspected the database CPU spike logged at 03:10 UTC, but that spike was caused by an unrelated nightly reporting job and had already resolved by 03:13 UTC, before the outage started. It was a red herring.

Resolution: Nadia manually renewed the certificate at 03:38 UTC; delivery resumed at 03:41 UTC once the change propagated. No payments were lost — webhook retries delivered all queued events by 04:10 UTC.

Follow-ups: (1) Re-enable auto-renewal for all webhook subdomains — owner: Nadia, due May 16. (2) Add a certificate-expiry alert 14 days before expiration — owner: Platform team, due May 23.

Postmortem: Halcyon API Elevated Error Rates
Incident ID: INC-2291 | Nimbusly Platform Engineering
Date of incident: June 3 | Report authors: Tomasz Kowalski, Aiko Tanaka

Summary
Between 09:12 and 10:47 UTC, the Halcyon public API returned 5xx errors for approximately 22% of requests. Internal dashboards and three enterprise customers (including Ferrovia Logistics) opened tickets during the window.

Timeline
- 09:12 — Error rate begins climbing on the /v2/orders endpoint.
- 09:15 — On-call engineer Aiko Tanaka is paged.
- 09:20 — Aiko's initial hypothesis: the 08:50 deploy of order-service v114 introduced the regression, since the timing lined up closely.
- 09:31 — order-service v114 is rolled back as a precaution. Error rate does not improve.
- 09:40 — Aiko escalates to Tomasz Kowalski.
- 09:45 — Tomasz pulls up recent infrastructure change tickets while investigating and flags the June 1 DNS change as worth checking.
- 09:52 — Tomasz notices that DNS lookups for the internal auth service are timing out intermittently, not order-service itself.
- 10:05 — Root cause identified: a DNS record TTL for auth.internal.nimbusly.com was set to 3600 seconds during a June 1 infrastructure change, but the resolver cache in the order-service pods was configured to cache for 24 hours, so pods were serving increasingly stale (and eventually unreachable) auth-service IPs as instances cycled.
- 10:20 — Fix deployed: resolver cache TTL overridden to match the DNS record.
- 10:47 — Error rate returns to baseline (<0.1%).

Root cause
Mismatched DNS caching configuration between the June 1 infrastructure change and the order-service pod resolver settings. The order-service v114 deploy on June 3 was unrelated and the rollback at 09:31 had no effect on the incident.

Customer impact
Three enterprise customers filed tickets: Ferrovia Logistics, Quanta Retail Group, and Marlowe & Finch. Of these, only Ferrovia Logistics experienced failed order submissions; the other two saw elevated latency but no failed requests, because their integrations use client-side retries.

Action items
1. Align resolver cache TTLs with DNS record TTLs across all internal services — owner: Tomasz, due June 17.
2. Add an alert for resolver-cache/DNS-TTL mismatches — owner: Aiko, due June 24.
3. Send a written RCA to Ferrovia Logistics — owner: Tomasz, due June 5.

What went well
The rollback of order-service v114, while ultimately not the fix, was a reasonable first step given the timing correlation and took under 15 minutes to execute.

Contributing factors
The June 1 infrastructure change that set the shorter DNS TTL was reviewed and approved through the standard change process, but the change ticket did not flag downstream services with long resolver-cache TTLs as an impacted dependency, so no one thought to check order-service's cache settings at the time.

Monitoring gap
There was no existing alert that compared a service's resolver-cache TTL against the DNS records it depends on, which is why the mismatch went undetected for two days before it caused visible errors.

state:
Nimbusly Platform - Changelog v4.0 through v4.3

v4.0 (Jan 8)
- New: GraphQL API (beta) alongside existing REST API. REST is not deprecated by this release.
- Breaking: Removed the /v1/reports endpoint (had been deprecated since v3.2). Use /v2/reports.
- Fixed: Timezone handling bug in scheduled exports.

v4.1 (Jan 22)
- New: SSO via SAML for Enterprise tier.
- Fixed: GraphQL beta occasionally returned stale cache data for up to 60 seconds after a mutation; now invalidates immediately.

v4.2 (Feb 5)
- New: Rate limits increased from 100 req/min to 250 req/min for all paid tiers. Free tier stays at 100 req/min, unchanged.
- Fixed: CSV export truncated rows beyond 50,000; limit raised to 500,000.

v4.3 (Feb 19)
- Breaking: GraphQL API exits beta and becomes the recommended API. REST API enters maintenance mode - it still works, but new features will only ship to GraphQL going forward.
- New: Audit log export now includes SSO login events (Enterprise tier).
- Deprecated: The sort_legacy query parameter on REST list endpoints; use sort instead. sort_legacy continues to function for now.

Known issues (as of v4.3)
- A small subset of SAML configurations created before v4.1 may need to be re-saved to pick up a metadata-URL fix; support can assist.

Migration guide
Clients on /v1/reports must move to /v2/reports (removed in v4.0). Clients relying on REST-only features should plan a GraphQL migration, though REST continues to function in maintenance mode as of v4.3. Free-tier clients should not expect the 250 req/min increase - that applies to paid tiers only.

v4.4 (Mar 5)
- New: Scheduled export jobs can now target GraphQL queries directly, not just REST.
- Fixed: Rate-limit counters occasionally under-counted burst traffic for endpoints behind the CDN cache; counts are now accurate.
- Deprecated: The v1 webhook payload format; v2 payload format becomes the default for new webhook subscriptions. Existing v1 subscriptions are unaffected until further notice.

Known issues (continued)
- A handful of Business-tier customers reported that CSV exports above 200,000 rows can time out in the browser; downloading via the API directly avoids this.

Support notes
Support has fielded an increase in tickets about the GraphQL migration since v4.3; the top question is whether REST will eventually be shut off. As of this changelog, there is no announced shutoff date for REST - it remains in maintenance mode indefinitely until further notice. Support recommends Enterprise customers with heavy REST usage schedule a GraphQL evaluation before the end of Q2 to stay ahead of any future roadmap changes.
